# Swamp Funk: Bass Drop — art plan (Phase C production visual set)

**Status (2026-09-26):** plan only. Nothing has been generated for Bass Drop except the paid probe batch `probe1` (8 jobs, 22 credits). Balance: **279.75 Higgsfield credits** (Plus plan). The container cannot download Higgsfield results yet (the egress policy blocks the CDN host), so **the probes are not reviewed and no batch below may start**: every batch uses approved images as references.

**Owner:** art track. **Machine-readable twin:** [`art/plan/bass-drop.json`](../../../art/plan/bass-drop.json), generated by [`art/plan/build_plan.py`](../../../art/plan/build_plan.py) from its row table and [`art/bible/artbible.json`](../../../art/bible/artbible.json) → `bassDrop`. If this page and the JSON disagree, the JSON wins; the asset table in §3 is spliced in from it.

Read with: [DESIGN.md](DESIGN.md) (when things play), [ANIMATION_SET.md](ANIMATION_SET.md) (every rig, slot and clip), [ART_BIBLE](../../ART_BIBLE.md) (the locks and gates), [prompt templates](../../../art/bible/prompts/README.md), [PIPELINE](../../PIPELINE.md) phases 1–3.

---

## 1. The look

**A neon bayou juke joint at party volume.** It is the Swamp Funk world (same room, symbols, outline and light rules, same hex HUD), rebuilt around sound:

- the reels sit between a **speaker stack** on the left, whose huge woofer *is* the Groove Meter, and **Baron Croak's DJ booth** on the right;
- two brass **horn speakers** are bolted on the top corners of the cypress frame and pump on every boom;
- **Gumbo** (heavyset adult alligator bouncer) leans on the lower cabinet; **Baron Croak** (lanky adult bullfrog DJ) slams the drop button;
- feature emblems: a **gold-and-teal jukebox** (Juke Jam) and a **crowned hot-pink speaker stack** (Mega Mix);
- everything that booms is a speaker: plum-black wood cabinets with gold bolts, charcoal cones, dark glass dust caps.

**The locks do not change** ([ART_BIBLE §3](../../ART_BIBLE.md#3-the-five-locks)):

| Lock | Value |
|---|---|
| Outline | Pure black `#000000`, ≈ 3% of the cell on symbols; 6–8 units at 2× on characters and props |
| Extrusion | Plum `#4B283D`, toward the lower right |
| Light | Key light top-left at 45°; 1 flat base + 2 hard shadow tones + 1 white specular streak; **no rim light, no baked glow, bloom, blur or cast shadow** |
| Camera | Symbols: frontal three-quarter, slight low angle. Mascots: three-quarter, turned toward the reels (Gumbo faces screen-right, Croak screen-left). Meter and cabinets: orthographic front (the woofer must be a true circle). **Exception:** the DJ booth is seen slightly from above so the platter reads |
| Canvas | Symbols on the 360×360 @2x canvas; every other rig at 2× its landscape design size (ANIMATION_SET §0); never upscale |

**Style formula:** pasted byte-identical into every image prompt by the renderer (`artbible.styleFormula`). Neon exists only in the environment. All glow (meter rim, button glow, LEDs, wild trail, title shine) is a runtime `fx_*` slot; art is painted flat.

**No words in art.** Titles, counts, WILD, ×N, prices and the game name are live text on `txt_*` slots or a typeset vector word-mark. The logo emblem is generated with a **blank banner**; a typographer sets SWAMP FUNK / BASS DROP on it.

**Hue watch-outs** (ART_BIBLE §4): H2 pink and W teal equal the background neon hues and must read as flat enamel; the meter trim band is generated light grey and recoloured per mode in code (teal / gold / pink); the multiplier badge is generated once in gold (t3) and hue-mapped to t1 teal, t2 lime, t4 orange, t5 pink (DESIGN §9).

**Key colours** (the same hex goes into the prompt and the keyer):

| Assets | Key | Why |
|---|---|---|
| H1–H4, meter, cabinets, horns, booth, W pieces, mega speaker emblem | `#00FF00` | no green in them |
| W (master, rig, parts), jukebox emblem (+ cracked), frame pieces, Gumbo | `#FF00FF` | teal or green content |
| Croak, notch icons, logo emblem | `#0000FF` | green + pink, or teal + pink, clash with both |

| High pays H1–H4 | Beauty masters (probed), rig-ready masters (P0), parts sheets (P1), H3 eye states (P1) | H2 shards, explode pieces: seeded Voronoi cut; `_blur` / `_glow` variants: `tools/matte/variants.py` |

| Feature emblems (`ui_feature_intro` / `_outro` / `_upgrade`) | Jukebox, crowned speaker stack (P0); jukebox crack state (P1) | Jukebox shards 1–6: Voronoi cut; banners and plates: vector |
| Logo | Emblem with a blank banner (P1) | Word-mark: typographer, vector; trademark search before release |
| Card art (`ui_intro_cards`, `ui_buy_cards`) | 3 intro illustrations (P1); 2 dedicated buy illustrations (P2) | Buy cards crop the intro art until P2; card frames: 9-slice of the frame texture + code neon edge |
| Backgrounds | Base landscape (probed), base portrait (P0), Juke Jam and Mega Mix variants in both orientations (P1), neon layers for the base plates (P1) and the variants (P2), game-tile plate (P2) | Variant neon: procedural extraction first; parallax layers: **cut** (the runtime pulses only the neon layer) |
| Mascots `chr_gumbo`, `chr_croak` | Design sheets (probed); per character: rig master (setup pose), body, head/face, hands, wardrobe/props sheets (all P0) | `fx_sweat`, `fx_note`: code; game-tile foreground: render the finished rigs |
| FX flipbooks | Optional look-dev key frames (P2) | Blender toon renders (PIPELINE phase 5); live-particle fallbacks at P0 |
| HUD, plates, chip, orbs, links, reticles, shadows, home markers | — | Existing Swamp Funk vector HUD; code-drawn `bd_ui` regions (ANIMATION_SET §8) |

Per row, the JSON adds the rendered prompt, its `promptHash`, the exact render command, the values and the bible path each came from, the key colour, output paths, the downstream steps, the gates and the fallback.

### How a row runs

1. **Render** (script-free): the row's `render` field, e.g. `python3 tools/gen/genlib.py render --template 'prop.txt#A' --var 'PROP=…' --var 'VIEW=…' --var 'DETAIL=…' --var 'KEY_HEX=#00FF00' --json`. It prints the prompt and its sha256 (`promptHash`); the renderer fails on an unfilled placeholder or a forbidden word. The Node twin (`tools/gen/lib/genlib.mjs`) prints the same bytes.
2. **Approve references** in [`art/plan/approvals.json`](../../../art/plan/approvals.json) (the chosen candidate's job id per row).
3. **Batch spec:** `python3 art/plan/build_plan.py spec --batch c01 > art/_work/hf-plans/bd_c01.spec.json`, then `pnpm gen:hf-ingest plan --spec art/_work/hf-plans/bd_c01.spec.json` prints the exact `generate_image_batch` call. Each candidate is its own job (`<row>.c1`, `<row>.c2`); references are passed as **Higgsfield job ids** (`medias: [{value: <job_id>, role: "image_references"}]`), so nothing local is uploaded.
4. **Generate** with the Higgsfield MCP, **always passing `model` explicitly**: the MCP's default image model is `gpt_image_2_5`, which is denylisted.
5. **Record + ingest** (`tools/gen/hf-ingest.mjs`, the ingestion track): `pnpm gen:hf-ingest record --plan … --from <MCP JSON>`, then `pnpm gen:hf-ingest` downloads into `art/_raw/<row id>/vNN/` and appends manifest rows.
6. **Review** against §6, pick, add the pick to `approvals.json`, then run the row's `downstream` steps (matte → cut/register → Spine) and the next batch.

**Model choice.** Nano Banana Pro everywhere, because consistency with the probes (made with it) matters more than price, and NB2 costs the same at 2k. The three H3 eye edits use **NB2 at 1k** (1.5 instead of 2 credits): they are edits of a head crop whose eyes are under 80 px on the 360 canvas. The hidden-area **fills** also use NB2, because it is the one model here with masked inpaint (`is_inpaint` + a `mask` media). Seedream and every other model are not used. **Never** any OpenAI model (`gpt_image_2`, `gpt_image_2_5`, `openai_hazel`): OpenAI's policy bars real-money gambling ([denylist](../../../licenses/denylist.json) `openai-gpt-image`). Higgsfield has no seed and no negative prompt, so consistency comes from the frozen formula plus the references.

**Resolution.** 2k for anything that ends ≤ ~1,300 units at the 2× authoring size (symbols, props, emblems, cards, rig masters, hand and prop sheets). 4k for background plates and for the mascot **body** and **face** sheets, whose pieces must reach the 2× authoring size after cutting (Croak is 1,260 units tall; a torso piece on a 2k sheet would need upscaling, which the bible forbids).

**Candidates.** 2 for anything that sets the look of later rows (rig masters, the W pieces, the meter, both emblems, notch icons, the mascot rig masters and body sheets); 1 for derived sheets and edits, which already have an approved image to follow.

**References** (≤ 4 per row, ordered identity first). Style anchors, once approved: `sym_H1` (gold, speaker cones), `sym_W` (teal enamel), `sym_H3` (character-like symbol); `sym_H2` for anything black and glossy. Backgrounds use the approved plate. Mascots use their approved design sheet for identity and, for B–E, the approved rig master for view and scale. Parts sheets and edits use the approved master as the **only** reference.

---

## 4. Budget

Measured prices (2026-09-26): NBP 2 credits at 2k, 4 at 4k; NB2 1.5 at 1k, 2 at 2k. Balance **279.75**. Retry allowance **1.5×** on P0 and P1 (the ART_BIBLE allows 2 regenerations per asset; in practice some rows need none).

| Pass | Base | With 1.5× retries | Reserves | Total | What it buys |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **P0** (first playable) | 88 | 132 | 18: probe redo 12 (two symbols + two sheets/plates), NB2 masked fills 6 | **150.0** (cap ~150) | Symbol + W rig masters, W pieces and parts, meter + parts, both feature emblems, notch icons, portrait base plate, both mascots' rig masters and four part sheets each |
| **P1** (feature-complete) | 74.5 | 111.75 | 6: NB2 masked fills | **117.75** | Symbol parts sheets, H3 eyes, lower cabinet, horns, booth, frame pieces, logo emblem, jukebox crack, three intro card illustrations, base neon layers, Juke Jam + Mega Mix plates |
| **P2** (polish) | 32 | — | — | 12 funded (`c21`), 20 unfunded (`c22`) | `c21`: tile plate, royal L1 test, right horn, two buy illustrations. `c22`: four variant neon layers, two FX look-dev frames |
| **Sum** | | | | **279.75** | 0.00 unallocated |

P0 by phase (base credits): symbols 16 · wild 10 · stage 6 · emblems 12 · backgrounds 4 · mascots 40. P1: symbols 12.5 · stage 26 · emblems 12 · backgrounds 24.

Unused retry allowance rolls forward: whatever P0 does not spend of its 44 retry credits funds P1, then `c22`.

**If the credits run out, cut in this order** (each row's `fallback` in the JSON says what replaces it):

1. `c22` (already unfunded): variant neon layers → procedural extraction of the neon hues from the plate; FX look-dev → Blender without an AI key frame.
2. `c21`: buy illustrations → crop the intro art; right horn → mirror the left one (its key light then reads upper right); royal test → royals stay plain vector; tile plate → brighten the base plate in code.
3. P1, cheapest loss first: frame pieces (keep the phase B code frame) · Juke Jam / Mega Mix **portrait** plates (colour-grade the base portrait in code) · base neon layers (procedural extraction) · card illustrations (composite the approved W, badges, emblem and meter over a background crop) · jukebox crack (procedural cracks) · H3 eye states (procedural lids) · logo emblem (typeset word-mark alone) · symbol parts sheets (SAM split + fills) · landscape variants (grade in code) · stage props last (they are on screen all the time).
4. P0 stays whole. Inside P0, drop the **second candidates** first, never a row: 32 credits in all (10 on the symbol and W rig masters, 14 on the W pieces, meter, emblems, icons and mascot rig masters, 8 on the two body sheets; cut them in that order, the body sheets last).

**Where a top-up goes** (the prompts README quotes $5 per 100 credits, expiring after 90 days; unverified): (1) restore any second candidates cut from P0; (2) `c22` (20); (3) second candidates for both mascot face sheets (+8) and the P1 prop masters' parts sheets (+6); (4) parallax layers only if the art director wants them after seeing the plates (3 × 4 credits per plate).

## 5. Order of operations

The order is style anchors → symbols → W → meter/cabinets/booth/horns → emblems → backgrounds → mascot parts, run once for P0, then again for P1 and P2. Each batch is one `generate_image_batch` call (≤ 12 jobs) and needs the listed batches **approved** first. Batches that do not depend on each other (for example `c07` needs only the probes) may be merged into one call to save review round-trips; the review order stays the same.

| Batch | Pass | Rows | Jobs | Credits | Needs approved |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `probe1` | P0 | review the 8 probes; approve the anchors | 0 | 0 (22 spent) | download of the probes |
| `c01` | P0 | H1–H4 rig-ready masters | 8 | 16 | probe1 |
| `c02` | P0 | W rig-ready master, W pieces | 4 | 8 | probe1 |
| `c03` | P0 | W parts sheet, meter master | 3 | 6 | probe1, c02 |
| `c04` | P0 | meter parts sheet, jukebox emblem | 3 | 6 | probe1, c03 |
| `c05` | P0 | crowned speaker stack emblem | 2 | 4 | probe1, c03, c04 |
| `c06` | P0 | notch icons, portrait base plate | 3 | 8 | probe1, c04, c05 |
| `c07` | P0 | Gumbo and Croak rig masters | 4 | 8 | probe1 (design sheets) |
| `c08` | P0 | both mascots' body, face, hands, props sheets | 10 | 32 | c07 |
| `c11` | P1 | H1–H4 parts sheets, H3 eye states | 7 | 12.5 | c01 |
| `c12` | P1 | lower cabinet, horn, booth masters, frame beam | 7 | 14 | probe1, c03 |
| `c13` | P1 | their parts sheets, frame post / sill / cap | 6 | 12 | c12 |
| `c14` | P1 | jukebox crack, logo emblem, 3 intro cards | 6 | 12 | probe1, c02–c05 |
| `c15` | P1 | base neon layers, Juke Jam + Mega Mix plates | 6 | 24 | probe1, c06 |
| `c21` | P2 | tile plate, royal L1 test, right horn, 2 buy cards | 5 | 12 | probe1, c02, c04, c05, c12 (+ an upload of the vector L1 render) |
| `c22` | P2 | variant neon layers, FX look-dev | 6 | 20 | c15 |

`python3 art/plan/build_plan.py summary` prints this table from the JSON.

**Downstream per family** (exact commands per row in the JSON):
- **Matte:** `GAME=bass-drop python3 tools/matte/outline_matte.py <raw> <out> --key <KEY> [--symbol <ID> | --no-fit]`. Beauty masters are canvas-fitted (`--symbol`, then `tools/matte/variants.py`); everything else keeps full resolution (`--no-fit`).
- **Cut and register:** each sheet is cut into pieces and every piece is registered to its master (ECC/SIFT), then named by the slot map in `artbible.bassDrop` (PIPELINE 3.1; `tools/split` is planned). Hidden overlaps the sheets missed are filled with `symbol_parts_sheet.txt#C` on NB2 masked inpaint (fill reserves).
- **Spine:** symbols through `tools/spine/gen.py` + `validate.mjs`; meter, env and characters in the Spine Editor (characters by a human animator, ANIMATION_SET §11), validated with `GAME=bass-drop node tools/spine/validate.mjs … --kind …` once CR-8 adds the `wild`, `ui`, `env` and `character` kinds.

## 6. Review rubric per asset

Gates are the [ART_BIBLE §10](../../ART_BIBLE.md#10-qa-gates) set (ids from `artbible.gates`; the JSON lists them per row). Automated first, then the art director. **Retry budget:** 2 regenerations per asset, then the best result goes to a human (paintover if needed).

| Kind (rows) | Automated gates | Art-director checks |
|---|---|---|
| **Symbol masters** (`sym_*`, `sym_*_rig`) | 64 px readability (both judges) · silhouette confusion < 0.85 IoU · palette ΔE ≤ 10 · outline 3–5 design px at the 124 px cell · halo = 0 · no text (OCR) · canvas/pivot · light reads top-left after the `restAngle` rotation | The rig-ready master is the **same object** as the approved beauty (flip test side by side); moving parts do not overlap; no motion blur; H3 mouth closed, eyes open |
| **Parts sheets** (`*_parts`, `sym_W_pieces`, `sym_H3_eyes_*`) | Rest-pose reassembly SSIM > 0.98, alpha IoU > 0.99, no holes at ±35° / ±15% · fills < 3 ΔE vs the visible part · halo · no text | Every listed piece appears exactly once; gaps between pieces so the key matte cuts them; rounded overlap caps where parts join; same scale and outline weight as the master; badge face and ribbon **blank** |
| **Stage props** (`bd_meter_*`, `bd_speaker_stack_*`, `bd_horn_*`, `bd_booth_*`, `frame_*`) | Palette ΔE · outline · style similarity · halo · no text · light top-left | Woofer is a true circle and the dust cap is blank (the counter is live text); no neon or glow painted; cone, cables, button, fader and platter read as separate parts; readable at display size (meter Ø 320, horn 116 × 100 design px) |
| **Emblems and icons** (`bd_emblem_*`, `bd_notch_icons`, `bd_logo_emblem`) | 64 px readability (icons read at 40 px, emblems at 120 px) · no text (**no pseudo-letters** on the jukebox or the logo banner) · palette ΔE · outline · halo · light | Jukebox and speaker stack differ in **silhouette**, not only colour (DESIGN §6.1); the logo banner is empty and wide enough for the word-mark; the crack edit changes nothing else |
| **Card illustrations** (`bd_card_*`) | No text · palette ΔE · style similarity · light | Subject inside the central two-thirds (crop test for both skins); objects match their approved references; backdrop darker and lower in contrast than the subject |
| **Backgrounds** (`bg_A_landscape`, `bd_bg_*`) | No text or readable signage (OCR) · darker central 60% (mean luminance below the edges) · palette ΔE · style similarity | Lower contrast and thinner lines than the foreground; neon masses at the far left and right (behind the mascots); portrait: key shapes inside the central 88% of the width (the 1:2 crop); **variants: every shape where the base has it** (edge-map IoU vs base, `layoutMatch`), so the crossfade does not swim; neon layers align with their plate |
| **Mascots** (`mascot_*_sheetA`, `chr_*`) | Adult proportions: head ≤ 0.27 of height, judged adult by both judges · identity vs the approved sheet (DINOv2, calibrate) · palette ΔE vs the mascot roles · outline 6–8 units at 2× · halo · no text · light | Nothing child-coded; correct facing (Gumbo right, Croak left); finger count constant; wardrobe matches the approved sheet (if the sheet has no chain, drop the chain from the part lists); every slot of ANIMATION_SET §5 present with the right near/far side (Gumbo near = his right, Croak near = his left); eye and mouth variants at identical size and angle |

## 7. Licence, provenance and the Higgsfield clearance caveat

- **Build and preview only.** `licenses/allowlist.json` → `higgsfield` has `clearance: pending`. Higgsfield outputs may be generated, matted, rigged and previewed, but **nothing made from them may ship** until the written clearance is filed in `licenses/clearances/` (training opt-out, real-money gambling use incl. EU/UK, output ownership and confidentiality, pass-through of Google's terms: [STACK § Image route](../../STACK.md#image-route-higgsfield-or-vertex--scenario-you-decide)).
- **The audit enforces it on `public/assets` today, not only at release.** `tools/licence/audit.mjs` fails on any file in `public/assets` whose manifest chain includes a licence that is not `cleared`, and on any shipped vendor generation with `tosVersion: null` (there is no `licenses/tos/higgsfield/` archive yet). Previews must load from `build/` or `art/source/`, never from `public/assets`, until then.
- **Manifest rows** (written by `pnpm gen:hf-ingest`): `route: "higgsfield-mcp"`, `vendor: "Higgsfield"`, `model` = the id the job reports (`nano_banana_2` for Nano Banana Pro), `seed: null`, `jobId`, `promptPath`, `promptHash`, `refHashes`, `licenseId: "higgsfield"`, `shipped: false`.
- **Model-id collision to watch:** a Nano Banana Pro job *reports* `nano_banana_2`, which is also the MCP id of Nano Banana 2. The requested MCP id is therefore kept in the ledger (`batch.model` / `request_model`); read it there, not from the row's `model`, when you need to know which model made an NB2 row.
- **No local uploads** in P0/P1: every reference is a Higgsfield job id. The only upload is the P2 royal test (our own vector render). This keeps unreleased mascots off Higgsfield's training-by-default exposure beyond what the probes already sent.
- **SynthID** is in every Nano Banana image and cannot be removed; decide a disclosure policy with counsel (ART_BIBLE §11). The paintover log and `humanEditor` / `humanEditSummary` fields are the authorship record.
- If the clearance does not come, the same rows run on **Vertex Nano Banana Pro** (`tools/gen/nbp.py`) with the same templates and hashes; only the references must be uploaded as files instead of job ids.

1. **Static board sprite vs the Spine rig.** Symbols show a static sprite and swap to a pooled Spine instance for actions (ANIMATION_SET §2.7). If the static sprite is the beauty master and the rig is built from the rig-ready master, the swap can pop. Recommendation: the board sprite is the matte of the approved **rig-ready** master (or the rig's setup pose rendered); the beauty master serves the paytable, card art and marketing.
2. **W design.** Bass Drop keeps the Swamp Funk proposal (gold-capped gator-tooth charm with teal inlay) and adds the ribbon, badge and clamps as separate pieces. Confirm before `c02`.
3. **Right horn:** mirrored (free; its key light reads upper right) or the P2 light-correct row.
4. **Card art:** generated illustrations (P1, 6 credits) or composites of approved pieces (free, flatter).
5. **Portrait plate:** reframe edit + width crop (planned, no outpaint credits) vs outpaint.
